hosting.// site: Named explicitly because the project holds a site whose id is not the project id. Without this, deploys target the default site (project-6ae60f7c-b11d-492a-bf9.web.app) instead of this one.
hosting.// headers: Order matters: the catch-all is first and the asset rule overrides it. Headers match the REQUESTED path, never the rewritten one, so a rule on /index.html only fires for a literal request to /index.html — which is the one path nobody asks for. Every real entry point (/ and every deep link) went to Firebase's default max-age=3600, so a returning operator could run the previous bundle for an hour after a deploy.
